classification.difficultyReason: Represent related perpendicular sides algebraically, form a quadratic using Pythagoras’ theorem and reject an inadmissible root.

content.prompt: A right-angled triangle has one side 7 cm longer than the side perpendicular to it. If the hypotenuse is 17 cm, find the side lengths of the triangle.

answer.worked:
Draw a right-angled triangle with perpendicular sides $x$ cm and $(x+7)$ cm and hypotenuse $17$ cm. By Pythagoras’ theorem:
$$\begin{align*}x^2+(x+7)^2&=17^2\\x^2+x^2+14x+49&=289\\2x^2+14x-240&=0\\x^2+7x-120&=0\\(x+15)(x-8)&=0\\x&=-15\text{ or }8.\end{align*}$$
A side length must be positive, so $x=8$. The other perpendicular side is $8+7=15$ cm. Hence the side lengths are $8$ cm, $15$ cm and $17$ cm.
